landmass.customize.title: Customize Landmass Terrain
landmass.customize.humidity.hint: Size of humidity zones in blocks: regions that are wet or dry overall. Vanilla Minecraft's are about %s blocks. Inside them, individual biomes keep the size set by Biome size, so a dry zone can still have some forest.
landmass.customize.biome_size.hint: Size of biomes compared with vanilla Minecraft, like the Large Biomes world type (400%). Terrain features such as hills, mountain ranges and coasts grow with them, so biomes keep matching the land.
landmass.preview.title: Preview
landmass.preview.hint: %s blocks per pixel. Drag to move, scroll to zoom.
landmass.preview.failed: Couldn't draw the map. See logs/latest.log.
landmass.configuration.title: Landmass
landmass.customize.zone.hot.hint: Width in blocks, from the equator. The hot band around the equator is twice this wide.
landmass.customize.zone.warm.hint: Width in blocks. Savannas, jungles and warm forests.
landmass.customize.zone.temperate.hint: Width in blocks. Plains and forests.
landmass.customize.zone.cold.hint: Width in blocks. Taiga and spruce forests.
landmass.customize.zone.frozen.hint: Width in blocks, from the edge of the frozen zone to the pole. Where the zones repeat past the pole, the polar band is twice this wide.
landmass.customize.zones_summary: Frozen zone starts %s blocks from the equator; pole at %s.
landmass.customize.custom_profile: The config's custom profile replaces these zone widths.
landmass.customize.spawn: Spawn: near %s, %s (picked on the preview map)
landmass.preview.spawn: Spawn: near %s, %s. Right-click to move it.
landmass.preview.spawn_auto: Spawn: picked by Minecraft. Right-click the map to pick it.
landmass.customize.continent_min.hint: Width in blocks of the smallest continents. Each continent picks a size between min and max, so they vary.
landmass.customize.continent_max.hint: Width in blocks of the largest continents. Neighbouring continents sometimes join into bigger landmasses.
landmass.customize.land_share.hint: How much of the world is land, counting islands; the rest is ocean. Less land means wider oceans between continents.
landmass.customize.archipelago_min.hint: Width in blocks of the smallest archipelagos: clusters and chains of islands, mostly out at sea.
landmass.customize.archipelago_max.hint: Width in blocks of the largest archipelagos.
landmass.customize.island_min.hint: Width in blocks of the smallest small islands. They fill the archipelagos, and a few are scattered across the open ocean.
landmass.customize.island_max.hint: Width in blocks of the largest small islands. The smaller ones are more common.
landmass.customize.continents.summary: Continents are about %s blocks apart, middle to middle.
landmass.customize.continents.off_summar: Land and oceans are left as Minecraft or your terrain mod makes them.
landmass.customize.island_biomes.hint: Size of biomes, humidity patches and local temperature changes on islands and archipelagos, compared with the continents. Lower makes island climates change faster.
landmass.customize.large_island_min.hint: Width in blocks of the smallest large islands: single islands between archipelagos and continents in size.
landmass.customize.large_island_max.hint: Width in blocks of the largest large islands.
landmass.customize.large_islands.hint: How common large islands are: 100%% is the usual number, 200%% twice as many, 0%% none.
landmass.customize.archipelagos.hint: How common archipelagos are: 100%% is the usual number, 200%% twice as many, 0%% none.
landmass.customize.islands.summary: Islands count towards the land share on the Continents page.
landmass.customize.coast_size.hint: Width of coasts, beaches and the bands from coast to inland, compared with vanilla Minecraft. Only used while Coast Size Override is on.
landmass.customize.feature.ravines.hint: Deep, narrow canyons cut into the ground.
The older winding cave tunnels, which often open as random holes in the ground. The big 1.18 caves (cheese, spaghetti and noodle caves) stay.
landmass.customize.feature.lava_lakes.hi: Pools of lava on the surface and underground.
landmass.customize.feature.aquifers.hint: Water sitting at its own level in dips and caves: random lakes on hillsides, flooded caves, and the lava at the bottom of the world. Off, caves are dry and only oceans and rivers hold water.
landmass.customize.feature.springs.hint: Single water and lava springs pouring out of cliffs and cave walls.
landmass.customize.terrain.summary: Terrain shape, height and mountains are left to vanilla or the installed terrain mod.
landmass.customize.structures.summary: Structures from other mods aren't affected. The World tab's Generate Structures turns all off.
landmass.customize.structure.temples.hin: Desert pyramids, jungle temples, witch huts and igloos.
landmass.customize.structure.ocean_struc: Ocean monuments, ocean ruins, shipwrecks and buried treasure.
landmass.customize.structure.strongholds: Strongholds. Without them there's no End portal and eyes of ender don't fly anywhere.
landmass.customize.structure.ruined_port: Ruined Nether portals in the overworld.
landmass.customize.structure.ancient_cit: Ancient cities in the deep dark.
landmass.customize.beyond.blocks: %s is past the recommended %s to %s blocks.
landmass.customize.beyond_elsewhere: A setting on the other page is past its recommended range.
landmass.customize.unsupported: Unsupported: may cause performance or compatibility issues.
landmass.preview.new_seed.hint: Re-roll a random seed and redraw the map. The new world gets this seed: it goes into the World tab's seed box.
landmass.customize.bridges.hint: How common land bridges (isthmuses) between neighbouring continents and islands are: 100% is the usual number, 200% twice as many, 0% none. Small islands in archipelagos get them too.
landmass.customize.bridge_width_min.hint: How wide a land bridge is at its narrowest, in blocks. Each bridge picks a width between min and max; bridges between small islands stay narrower than the islands.
landmass.customize.bridge_width_max.hint: How wide the widest land bridges are at their narrowest, in blocks. Big ones only form between landmasses big enough for them.
landmass.customize.bridge_length.hint: The widest stretch of water a land bridge or island chain crosses, in blocks. Raise it to join continents across wider seas.
landmass.customize.chains.hint: How many of the land bridges come as a chain of islands instead of solid land.
landmass.customize.bars.hint: How much of the coastline has sand bars: spits that leave the shore, run along the coast and curl back at their tips, and barriers that close off lagoons. All sit on wide shallow shoals. 100% is the usual amount, 0% none.
landmass.customize.bar_width.hint: How wide sand bars are near the shore, in blocks. Spits narrow toward their tips; they reach about three to ten widths out from the shore.
landmass.customize.bar_length.hint: Roughly how far one sand bar runs along the coast, in blocks. Each picks a length from about half to one and a half times this.
landmass.customize.bridge_islets.hint: How many sandbank islets lie in the shallows beside land bridges and trail off the tips of bridges that don't quite reach across. 0% for none.
landmass.customize.lagoons.hint: How many of the sand bars are barriers joined to the shore at both ends, closing off a shallow lagoon (often with an inlet), instead of spits.
landmass.customize.bar_islets.hint: How many small sandbank islets lie off sand bars: a trail past the tip of each spit and a few on the seaward side. 0% for none.
landmass.customize.straits.hint: How common straits are: narrow channels of sea cutting between continents and large islands where they meet, splitting them apart. 100% is the usual number, 0% none.
landmass.customize.strait_width_min.hint: How wide a strait is at its narrowest, in blocks. Each strait picks a width between min and max, and stays well under the size of the land it cuts.
landmass.customize.strait_width_max.hint: How wide the widest straits are at their narrowest, in blocks. They widen toward the open sea at both ends.
landmass.customize.coasts.page.bridges.h: Isthmuses and island chains between neighbouring landmasses.
landmass.customize.coasts.page.bars.hint: Spits, lagoon barriers, shoals and sandbank islets along coasts.
landmass.customize.coasts.page.straits.h: Narrow channels of sea between landmasses that meet.
landmass.customize.coasts.summary: Bridges join landmasses, straits split them; bars and erosion shape coasts.
landmass.customize.waviness.hint: How wavy the borders between temperature zones are. 0% keeps them perfectly straight (biomes still mix a little right along them); higher values make the bands meander north and south more and more, like real climate zones. 100% is the default.
landmass.customize.coasts.page.erosion.h: Coasts worn into jagged headlands, coves, bays and inlets, so landmasses look less rounded.
landmass.customize.mainland_erosion_rate: How much of the continents' coastline is eroded into headlands, coves, bays and inlets. 0% leaves every coast smooth, 100% erodes all of it.
landmass.customize.mainland_erosion_inte: How deep and rugged erosion is on continents: how far bays and inlets cut inland and headlands stick out. 100% is the default; scales with the size of the continents.
landmass.customize.mainland_erosion_vari: How much the erosion intensity changes along the continents' coasts. At 50% some stretches get half the set intensity and others one and a half times it; 0% keeps it even everywhere.
landmass.customize.island_erosion_rate.h: How much of the islands' coastline (large islands, archipelagos and small islands) is eroded. 0% leaves every coast smooth, 100% erodes all of it.
landmass.customize.island_erosion_intens: How deep and rugged erosion is on islands. 100% is the default; scales with the size of each kind of island.
landmass.customize.island_erosion_variat: How much the erosion intensity changes along the islands' coasts, from island to island and along each one. At 50% it ranges from half to one and a half times the set intensity; 0% keeps it even.
landmass.customize.deviation_temperature: Biome Temperature Zone Deviation: how many temperature zones (hot, warm, temperate, cold, frozen) a deviation patch can jump, colder or warmer. At 2 a hot desert can turn up in a temperate area; at 4 or 5 a snowy patch can turn up in the tropics. Bigger jumps are rarer than small ones. 0 turns temperature jumps off. Default 1.
landmass.customize.deviation_humidity.hi: Biome Humidity Zone Deviation: how many humidity bands (Minecraft has five, arid to humid) a deviation patch can jump, drier or wetter, like a rain-shadow desert in jungle country or a wet pocket in dry land. 0 turns humidity jumps off. Default 1.
landmass.customize.deviation_size.hint: The typical width of a deviation patch in blocks; each is between about 0.7 and 1.3 times this, with ragged edges. Default 3,000, which at the default zone sizes is about the size of real-world climate oddities like the Atacama or Namib deserts.
landmass.customize.deviation_frequency.h: How much of the world lies in deviation patches. 0% turns them off. Default 5%, roughly how much of real land has a climate out of step with its latitude (cold deserts, rain shadows, cool coasts). Above about 20% patches start to overlap.
landmass.customize.desert_share.hint: Roughly how much of the hot zone is desert; the rest is savanna, forest and jungle. Default 45%. 50% gives deserts and wet land in equal measure. How big each desert is follows the humidity zone size on the Zones page. Has no effect if tropics is set to DESERT in the config.
landmass.customize.deviation.summary: Patches where the climate jumps zones, like a snowy forest beside a desert.
landmass.customize.presets.summary: Presets set everything at once. Yours are saved in config/landmass-presets.
landmass.customize.presets.name: Name for a new preset
landmass.customize.presets.save.hint: Saves every setting on this screen, on all tabs, as a preset under the name typed on the left. A preset with the same name is replaced.
landmass.customize.presets.load.hint: Loads this saved preset: every setting on every tab. Nothing changes until you press Done.
landmass.customize.presets.delete.hint: Deletes this saved preset. Click twice to confirm.
landmass.customize.presets.need_name: Type a name for the preset first.
landmass.customize.presets.save_failed: Couldn't save the preset; the game log says why.
landmass.customize.presets.loaded: Loaded %s. Check the other tabs or the preview, then press Done.
landmass.customize.preset.default.hint: The mod's defaults: continents 6,000 to 24,000 blocks, 100,000 blocks from the equator to the frozen zone, vanilla-sized biomes.
landmass.customize.preset.vanilla.hint: Everything at about vanilla's scale: landmasses 1,000 to 4,000 blocks, climate zones a couple of thousand blocks wide, vanilla biomes, smaller coastal features.
landmass.customize.preset.large_biomes.h: Four times vanilla, like the Large Biomes world type: biomes at 400%, landmasses 4,000 to 16,000 blocks.
landmass.customize.preset.xl.hint: Landmasses in the tens of thousands of blocks (24,000 to 96,000), 400,000 blocks from the equator to the frozen zone, larger biomes and coastal features.
landmass.customize.preset.xxl.hint: Landmasses up to a couple of hundred thousand blocks (58,000 to 230,000), 960,000 blocks from the equator to the frozen zone and the pole about 1.2 million blocks out.
landmass.customize.preset.xxxl.hint: Landmasses in the hundreds of thousands of blocks (150,000 to 600,000), 2.5 million blocks from the equator to the frozen zone.
landmass.customize.preset.realistic.hint: Earth's scale at 1 block = 1 metre: continents 1.2 to 4.8 million blocks, Earth's climate zones (10 million blocks from equator to pole), 29% land, coastal features sized like real ones. Days of travel; meant for exploring.
landmass.customize.coasts.page.shores.hi: What the coasts are like: long stretches of sandy or gravel beach, grassy shores, rocky shores and cliffs, instead of Minecraft's patchy beaches.
landmass.customize.shore_beaches.hint: How much of the coast is beaches, compared with the other kinds of shore. Set every kind to 0% to leave coasts as Minecraft picks them.
landmass.customize.shore_gravel.hint: The part of beaches that are gravel (shingle) instead of sand.
landmass.customize.shore_grassy.hint: How much of the coast has the land's own ground (grass, forest floor, snow...) running straight into the sea, without a beach.
landmass.customize.shore_rocky.hint: How much of the coast is low, rocky stony shore.
landmass.customize.shore_cliffs.hint: How much of the coast is cliffs: rocky shore with the land climbing steeply right behind it.
landmass.customize.shore_stretch.hint: Roughly how long one stretch of a kind of shore runs along the coast, in blocks.
landmass.world_map.title: World map
landmass.world_map.hint: %s blocks per pixel. Drag to move, scroll to zoom, right-click to teleport.
landmass.world_map.no_permission: Teleporting needs cheats on, the same as /tp.
landmass.world_map.unavailable: The map only works in singleplayer or when you host the LAN world.
landmass.customize.page.zones.hint: Temperature zone widths, humidity zone size, biome size and band waviness.
landmass.customize.page.deviation.hint: Climate deviation patches, where the climate jumps warmer, colder, drier or wetter, and how much of the hot zone is desert.
landmass.customize.page.continents.hint: Custom Landmass Generation, continent sizes and how much of the world is land.
landmass.customize.page.islands.hint: Large islands, archipelagos and small islands: their sizes and how common they are.
landmass.customize.page.coasts.hint: Land bridges, sand bars, straits, coastal erosion and shore types, and a switch for all of them.
landmass.customize.landmass_generation.h: On: Landmass places continents, islands and oceans with the sizes on these pages. Off: the land and oceans of vanilla Minecraft, or of the installed terrain mod or datapack, are kept. Climate settings apply either way.
landmass.customize.coast_override.hint: On: coasts, beaches and the bands from coast to inland get the size below. Off: coast size is left to vanilla Minecraft or the installed terrain mod or datapack.
landmass.customize.coastline.hint: On: land bridges, sand bars, straits, coastal erosion and the shore type mix on these pages shape the coastlines. Off: coastlines are just the continents' and islands' own outlines, and beaches are left to vanilla Minecraft or the installed terrain mod.
landmass.customize.coastline.off_summary: Coastline features are off, so these settings are not used.
landmass.customize.landmass.off_summary: Custom Landmass Generation is off (Continents page), so these settings are not used.
